additionalCoursework:
Recommended subject areas to support medical school academics and/or MCAT success: genetics, immunology, molecular biology, physiology, anatomy, statistics, organic chemistry, and physics

All coursework must be less than 10 years old at the time of application, have a grade of "C-" or higher, and must be from a regionally accredited college/university in the United States.

*For full details on pre-reqs, please visit https://www.unlv.edu/medicine/admissions/primary-application#courses

medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
Voluntary Leave of Absence or Voluntary Health Withdrawal

Students may request a Voluntary Leave of Absence for personal or family reasons. Students must be in good academic standing and not subject to academic actions or professionalism violations to be eligible for a voluntary leave of absence. The request must be presented in writing to the Senior Associate Dean for Student Affairs and Admissions in a timely manner. Students must indicate the reason for requesting a leave of absence as well as an expected time the student anticipates returning to full-time academic status.

A student may seek a Voluntary Leave of Absence for Medical Reasons (Voluntary Health Withdrawal). This request must be submitted in writing to the UNLV Health Withdrawal Committee. A copy of the process and forms for submitting a Request for Voluntary Health Withdrawal are online. The Voluntary Health Withdrawal Committee will make a recommendation to the School of Medicine Senior Associate Dean for Student Aff
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are numerous student organizations on campus serving specialty interests and advancement as well as traditional student organizations.  Active chapters of AOA, AMA, AMSA, SNMA, LMSA, CMDA, APAMSA, Phi Delta Epsilon, Gold Humanism, and more.  Student interest clubs and intramural sports teams are active and supported by the medical school's wellness programming. Student government positions by cohort are also available along with elected positions on school committees and in Learning Communities. Students may also serve as ambassadors to the school for outreach to pre-medical populations or K-12 STEM exploration.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most students live off-campus in rental housing or with family. There are no dorms or campus housing.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Qlub Med is a school organization that serves gender and sexual minority students at the Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
We believe in creating a welcoming student-centered culture that focuses on direct interaction, support, and programming for individuals to thrive in an academic medicine setting and beyond. Our school has Learning Communities, Student Government, and a vast array of professional and social organizations/clubs. Well-being programming is also robust, which includes dedicated mental health services for medical students. Administration, Faculty, and Staff are readily available, and services and support includes specialty offices such as Academic Support, Student Financial Services, Career Services, Student Research, and Community Affairs. The school houses a dedicated gym for students, along with a Medical Library. Students may also access all offerings and facilities on the UNLV main campus.
For more information visit: https://www.unlv.edu/medicine/student-life
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Las Vegas has very limited public transportation and clinical curriculum occurs all around the city. There are also opportunities for work in the school's free clinic, with other community service entities, and with various research locations within the valley. The Cost of Attendance considers this extra driving requirement and provides additional funds for vehicle wear and tear/operation.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional dress is required for patient interactions and clinical experiences. If scrubs are required, they will be provided by the clinical facility or the school.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV Office of Academic Support offers one-on-one learning advising, group study sessions, workshops, national testing preparation, and peer tutoring.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Most courses are conducted in a small group format. Problem Based Learning and experiential clinical skills training are highlighted in the curriculum along with gross and virtual anatomy.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV provides medical students with an intensive, hands-on educational experience - one grounded in small group work and the community, across all four years. Students completing the Kerkorian School of Medicine's educational program will be fully prepared to start a rewarding career in medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Not Applicable - students may pick from any specialty, including primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Each student has access to apply for school and university funds to support resources and services associated with research activities, including, but not limited to, publishing and presenting at national conferences. Research can be done both locally and nationally.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Public academic system overseen by the Nevada Board of Regents. UNLV is a minority-serving institution with Carnegie R1 distinction.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students participate in community service during all four years of medical study.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is readily available to those who wish to pursue it. Fundamental research skills are taught in Phase 1 as part of the foundational training.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: University Medical Ctr, Sunrise Hospital, VA Hospital, O'Callaghan Military Medical Ctr at Nellis, Southern Hills Hospital, Mountain View Hospital, Valley Hospital, Dignity Health - St. Rose

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Our vision is to create a world-class center of excellence and innovation for medical education, patient care, community service, and research that prepares Nevada's physicians with the most advanced knowledge, treatments, and technologies while serving the health care needs of our diverse state and urban communities.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV is a LCME accredited, full-scale, four-year allopathic medical school that is an integral part of a vibrant, research-intensive public university. The medical school's mission is to improve access to high-quality health care in Nevada by increasing the number of physicians and trained specialists who are committed to serving the region. One of the primary goals of the Kerkorian School of Medicine is to provide diverse and medically underserved populations access to timely, high-quality health care. The accompanying academic health center serves as the core infrastructure for the entire medical community and generates top-quality research that spans the basic and clinical sciences.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters must be on official letterhead and signed by each letter writer either through wet signature or a certified digital signature (e.g. Docusign, Adobe digital signature, etc.). A minimum of 3 letters must be received by the application deadline of October 1st.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letter writers should be from individuals directly related to professional experiences (education, community, clinical, research, employment, military, etc.) or from a formal pre-medical committee (i.e. packet style). It is strongly recommended to have a physician letter.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interview experiences are placed into a designated week chosen by the applicant upon invitation.  There is a required asynchronous video component and then required virtual live sessions including small group, large group, and 1:1.  Optional in-person building tours of the medical school are also available to interviewees throughout the cycle.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Standardized interview, fully virtual, semi-closed file (qualitative information only - no quantitative)
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants meeting initial screening criteria will be sent the URL to access the secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Recommended within 14 days of invitation and no later than November 15th.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Preference is given to Nevada residents and out-of-state applicants with significant ties to Nevada or those who are from select western states. Details about qualifying appear on our website.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Preference is given to out of state applicants with significant connections to Nevada or those who are legal residents of a listed western region state. Visit our website for details.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: DACA applicants will be reviewed on a case by case basis with preference given to Nevada residents who hold specific documents to aid with degree matriculation and training.

Announcements for Admissions
The following exceptions and considerations are taken into consideration regarding requirements to the Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV application process due to past events and global circumstances. When developments or changes occur, we will continue to update this website with information for applicants. Additional important reminders are also posted here.

MCAT Test Scores
All applicants who submitted an AMCAS application into the open cycle for UNLV must take the MCAT no later than October 1 to maintain eligibility in that cycle. This includes any retakes intended for the cycle in order to meet the minimum score of 499. There are no exceptions for late testing or scores that do not meet the minimum. 

Online Prerequisite Coursework
The Kerkorian School of Medicine accepts any instruction delivery format for our required prerequisites for application. This means the course can be taken in-person, hybrid, or online. Courses must still be from a U.S. college/university that is regionally accredited and need to be less than 10 years old at the time of application.

Pass/Fail Prerequisite Coursework
Consideration for prerequisite courses that were graded as pass/fail or satisfactory/unsatisfactory due to COVID-19 may be accepted from the following semesters without prejudice: Winter 2020, Spring 2020, Summer 2020, Fall 2020, Winter 2021, Spring 2021, Summer 2021, Fall 2021. Consideration for prerequisite courses that were graded as pass/fail or satisfactory/unsatisfactory due to the December 2024 shooting at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas may be accepted without prejudice for the Fall 2024 semester. If you are applying from a school that had a similar tragedy that also resulted in a pass/fail grade on a prerequisite instead of a letter grade, please email the office of admissions at the time of your application. For more information on how pass/fail affects the AMCAS GPA calculation, please visit their website.

Application Deadline
AMCAS applications may be submitted until October 1 each cycle. For an interactive calendar related to the AMCAS process, please visit the AAMC website. You may submit an AMCAS application to the Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV if you have an anticipated MCAT test date that is occurring by October 1. We will wait for your score to come in. Similarly, you can also submit if you have letters of recommendation pending. Again, we will wait for those to arrive, however at least three qualifying letters must be in by October 1. UNLV is no longer participating in the Early Decision Program. Applicants who have a strong interest in UNLV should simply apply early in the cycle.

Interviews 
The Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV has permanently gone to a fully virtual interview process with components that are both asynchronous and virtual-live in nature. For more information, please visit our Interview Days page.

For questions or concerns, please email admissions@medicine.unlv.edu
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Kerkorian School of Medicine takes the latest score as the official score.  We do not take the highest or an average.  We do not recommend taking the MCAT more than three times, however you will not be disqualified if you do have more than three. The MCAT score must be less than 3 years old at the time of application.  The committee does receive viewing rights to all scores attempted in order to assess the progression of success.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: 499 from the latest score and there are no exceptions
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: 3.2 Cumulative and a 3.2 BCPM from a regionally accredited college/university in the United States
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The last two years of study will be assessed for continued academic success, but the junior and senior year cannot replace a low undergraduate GPA that doesn't meet our minimum cumulative and BCPM requirements. Applicants below the minimums from undergraduate work may complete post-bacc or graduate work for consideration. At least 30 credit hours of BCPM at a 3.2 or higher in post-bacc or graduate study at a regionally accredited school in the United States is required to remain eligible. Cumulative overall GPA must also be at 3.2 or higher. Courses in progress at the time of application are not officially calculated into the candidate's GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: It is required to have at least 30 BCPM credit hours post-bacc with strong grade trends (3.2 or higher) to combat a low undergraduate GPA.  Additional BCPM credit hours up to 60 will continue to demonstrate academic success and are preferred.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Prerequisites for medical school application may be taken at a community college but must be completed separately from high school credit/diploma application and must be less than 10 years old at the time of graduation with a grade of C- or higher.  CLEP, AP, or Audit coursework is not accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may email updates to the Office of Admissions solely for significant advancements in clinical experiences or community service that have occurred since the time of primary application. Applicants with prerequisites in progress at the time of primary application must also email an unofficial transcript to provide proof of their final grade earned.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Technical standards are reflected online and in the student handbook. The Office of Admissions does provide the technical standards with attestation requirements at the time of Secondary Application submission and again at admitted applicant onboarding. The Office of the Registrar will require annual attestations starting at orientation. Those who may need accommodations should work with the Office of Student Affairs and the representative for the school of medicine from the UNLV Office of Disability Resources Center.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Required courses by the Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV include the following:
- Biology: three courses; one course must have laboratory experience
- Biochemistry: one course
- Behavioral Science/Psychology or Sociology: one course

Students cannot use AP, CLEP or Audit credits to satisfy the required premedical coursework. 
Pass/fail also not accepted (*COVID exceptions do apply within 2020/2021. Please see our policy.)

Premedical courses in progress must be occurring in Summer or Fall of the admissions cycle (completed by December of the admissions cycle).

- Full details are on the medical school premedical requirement website: https://www.unlv.edu/medicine/admissions/primary-application
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: May 2016. Prerequisite coursework must have been completed within 10 years of application submission. Prerequisites can be in progress at the time of submission (summer or fall terms graded by Dec)
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Priority is given to applicants who are residents of Nevada, applicants with significant personal or family connections to Nevada, and applicants from select western states.

Please visit our website for the most current information on residency for application, minimum qualifications, and quantitative/qualitative requirements.
 
https://www.unlv.edu/medicine/admissions/applicants
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Clinical experience is required and can be fulfilled by traditional shadowing or another volunteer/paid method such as scribing, medical assisting, nursing, medical translation/interpreter, etc.. Clinical experiences should be longitudinal in nature with significant exposure/work with a physician who is actively seeing/treating patients. Candidates should clearly outline the physician interaction and demonstrate its majority presence in the experience.
